concepts.name: 3.10 X | Y union types
concepts.description: Python 3.10 allows union types to be written with |, such as str | None, instead of typing.Optional or typing.Union.

concepts.description: Python 3.10 officially supports grouping multiple context managers across lines inside parentheses after with.

questions.prompt: Match only user events whose id value is an int, and capture the id.

content.template:
# event is a dict such as {'type': 'user', 'id': 42}.
match event:
    case {'type': 'user', 'id': {{answer}}}:
        handle_user(user_id)
    case _:
        pass

questions.explanation: Python 3.10 structural pattern matching can destructure mappings, sequences, and class instances while binding selected values. case {'type': 'user', 'id': int(user_id)}: ... both checks the event shape and captures an integer id. A capture name by itself matches almost anything; use literal/class/subpattern structure when validation is intended.

questions.prompt: Use Python 3.10 union syntax for a nullable string.

content.template:
def normalize(value: {{answer}}) -> str:
    return '' if value is None else value.strip()

questions.explanation: Python 3.10 allows union types to be written with |, such as str | None, instead of typing.Optional or typing.Union. def parse(value: str | bytes) -> str: ... uses the compact union syntax. The | syntax is a type expression here; it should not be confused with the unrelated set/dict union operator used on runtime values.

questions.prompt: Open both resources in one parenthesized with statement.

accepted_answers: with (open(src) as inp, open(dst, 'w') as out):

questions.explanation: Python 3.10 officially supports grouping multiple context managers across lines inside parentheses after with. with (open(src) as inp, open(dst, 'w') as out): ... keeps a long multi-resource with statement readable. All context managers are still entered left-to-right and exited in reverse order.
